defects.summary: rz-diff side ownership is trusted unconditionally although stock Rizin 0.9.1 swaps original/modified when the older file has exactly one recovered function; the quarantine written for this exists only on unmerged branches.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/secondary/rzdiff.py:119-120 (original -> older, modified -> newer, no cardinality guard); guard absent on main (`git grep rzdiff_orientation_unverified main` is empty) but present at b58bb53d:src/patchtrace/secondary/reconcile.py:66 and b58bb53d:src/patchtrace/unified/compute.py:55; real stock output origin/qualify/native-cli-seeding-20261105:docs/qa/native-cli-20261105/seeded-stock-elf-pair-1-2.stdout.log
defects.failure_scenario: Older artifact with one recovered function, newer with two: stock rz-diff emits `{"original": sym.helper@0x401013 (a NEWER-only function), "modified": entry0@0x401000}`. parse_output accepted exactly that text in this pass and stored older_address=0x401013. reconcile then reports a wrong-side disagreement/agreement (secondary/evidence.py adds +8 or marks `contested`), and unified atoms carry swapped RVAs. Identical JSON is produced for the 1:2 and 2:1 inputs, so the stored set cannot be told apart afterwards.
defects.proposed_fix: Spec first (docs/specs/secondary-engine.md): refuse, never swap. When the modified side holds at most one distinct function across matched and one-sided rows, raise PT-SECONDARY-ORIENTATION (kind `rzdiff-singleton-ownership`) for producers without a qualified ownership fix; keep every other shape unchanged. Do not port the version-wide quarantine without an owner decision.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_secondary_rzdiff.py: parametrised over the four retained stdout shapes (1:1, 1:2, 2:1 refused; 2:2 and corrected 1-original/2-modified accepted) plus a scheduler-level test that the run is `failed` with error_code PT-SECONDARY-ORIENTATION and nothing is published.

defects.summary: rz-diff probe can raise instead of reporting `unsupported`; the default-engine probe in `secondary run` is unguarded.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/secondary/rzdiff.py:56 (catches OSError/ValueError only), rzdiff.py:52 and :148 (TemporaryDirectory without ignore_cleanup_errors), src/patchtrace/secondary/cli_run.py:73
defects.failure_scenario: jobs.run_process raises RuntimeError("PT-BACKEND: terminated child did not exit") or Windows cannot delete the probe scratch: `patchtrace secondary run PROJECT` (no --engine) ends with a traceback instead of an unsupported engine row. Reproduced the RuntimeError escape with an injected runner.
defects.proposed_fix: Catch RuntimeError in rzdiff.probe, use ignore_cleanup_errors=True, and wrap the default-engine probe loop in cli_run.execute like evidence_panel_service.probe_engines does.

defects.summary: SEC-8 still open: rz-diff stdout is decoded lossily and any U+FFFD is treated as invalid UTF-8.
defects.failure_scenario: A function name that legitimately contains U+FFFD (valid UTF-8 EF BF BD) makes the whole run fail with "rz-diff output is not valid UTF-8"; the digest is computed over re-encoded text rather than the captured bytes.
defects.proposed_fix: Use ProcessResult.log_bytes (jobs.py:51) in RzDiffAdapter.run, decode strictly in parse and hash the raw bytes.

defects.summary: A file in which rz-diff finds no functions is reported as a generic input error.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/secondary/rzdiff.py:102; real stderr `No functions found in file0` with exit 0 and empty stdout in origin/qualify/native-cli-seeding-20261105:docs/qa/native-cli-20261105/README.md
defects.failure_scenario: Unsupported or function-less binary: the run is `failed [PT-SECONDARY-INPUT] rz-diff produced no output`; the user cannot tell an unsupported binary from a broken tool without opening the stored stderr tail.
defects.proposed_fix: When stdout is empty and stderr contains the fixed "No functions found in file" marker, raise PT-SECONDARY-INPUT with kind `no-functions` and a message naming the side.

defects.summary: The .BinDiff importer has no row cap: a hostile or corrupt database can exhaust memory before the 120 s deadline.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/secondary/bindiff.py:226-240 (unbounded loop building one pydantic record per `function` row); limits are only the 512 MiB file size (bindiff.py:35) and the wall clock (bindiff.py:38). tasks/todo.md:123 lists "Importer per-table row caps" as open.
defects.failure_scenario: A user imports a 512 MiB .BinDiff holding ~10 million minimal `function` rows through `secondary import-bindiff` or the Engine evidence dialog. Measured here on synthetic rows: about 1.4 KB per SecondaryMatch and more than 60,000 rows per second, so several GB are allocated inside the GUI or CLI process before the deadline fires; the 32 MiB store-row limit only rejects the result afterwards.
defects.proposed_fix: Spec first (docs/specs/bindiff-execution.md section 7.2): `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM function` against a MAX_FUNCTION_ROWS constant before the loop (and a counter inside it), raising PT-SECONDARY-LIMIT.

defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/secondary/bindiff_probe.py:157 (only `probe-cancelled` is excluded), :177 and :186 (timeout and spawn errors become `probe-failed`); clear_probe_cache is never called from src/

defects.proposed_fix: Mirror the intel-tools TA-10 fix: let _probe return (report, cacheable) and skip caching when the version or help run ended with a reason or a spawn exception; give the timeout its own kind/message.
